youtube.title: Why We Pour Salt on Icy Roads 🧂 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Ice always has a thin film of liquid water on its surface. Road salt dissolves into that film and lowers the freezing point of the water. Salty water has to be colder than zero degrees Celsius to freeze, so the ice keeps melting. It stops working in extreme cold, below about minus 9 degrees Celsius for regular rock salt.
